data.why: The repo's own bundled sample (assets/sample/sample.out.gnu) is ~6200 lines (well over the 200KB budget), so a smaller synthetic QE-format band file with the same two-column (k-distance, energy eV) layout and blank-line-separated bands was written, sized to show a clean 1.5 eV direct gap at k=0.5.

goals: Upload a Quantum ESPRESSO .dat.gnu band-structure file and see the bands plotted
Set the Fermi energy and see the plotted energies shift relative to it
Mark high-symmetry k-points with labels on the x-axis
Compute and display the band gap between the valence and conduction bands
Customize plot styling (colors, line thickness, markers, axis labels, grid) and preview the change
Export the band structure plot as an image file

review.summary: The tree is faithful to the README and to the app's own how-to: plot a QE band file relative to E_F, label high-symmetry points, read the band gap, style and export. The evidence holds up apart from one wrong citation. Before filing, it needs a core loader/plotter feature, gap wording that matches the code's nearest-points-around-E_F method, that citation fixed, and the trivial clear-data phase folded in or dropped.
